entries.title: How can a quilt tell a story?
entries.answer: Artist Faith Ringgold made artworks that brought pictures, words, and fabric together. A story quilt can have a picture in the middle and written pieces around it, with patterned cloth framing what you read and see. You might notice a neighborhood or a person in the image, then read about a moment in that person’s life. Ringgold used cloth as a real part of the storytelling, including its colors, texture, and borders.
facts: Faith Ringgold’s picture book Tar Beach grew out of her story-quilt work.

entries.title: How can shading make a picture look solid?
entries.answer: A ball under a lamp has a bright part facing the lamp and a darker part turned away from it. An artist can draw those changes in lightness inside a flat circle so it looks like a ball. The change from light to dark is often gradual on a rounded surface. The ball may also leave a darker shape on the table behind it, where it blocks some light.
facts: Artists use the word value to talk about how light or dark a part of a picture is.

entries.title: How can small pieces make a big picture?
entries.answer: Mosaics use small pieces of glass, stone, or another material arranged into a picture or pattern. Each piece can cover just a little bit of the final surface. From far away the pieces may look like a single picture. From close up you can see each piece, the gaps, and how colors were grouped. A mosaic artist can turn pieces to follow the curves of a face, flower, or animal.
facts: A small piece used to make a mosaic is called a tessera.

entries.title: How did Alma Thomas make pictures out of patches of color?
entries.answer: Alma Thomas painted groups of bright marks that can look as if they are moving in rows, rings, or streams. Small spaces between the marks let quieter colors show. She could change the feeling of a picture by changing the order of the colors or the direction the marks seemed to move. Some of her paintings drew ideas from gardens, light, and space without trying to copy a view exactly.
facts: Alma Thomas taught art in Washington, D.C., before devoting more time to her painting.

entries.title: How did Georgia O’Keeffe make small things feel huge?
entries.answer: Georgia O’Keeffe painted flowers, hills, bones, buildings, and other things she looked at closely. In some flower paintings, a small petal fills a large part of the picture. A viewer can study shapes and curves that might usually go unnoticed while passing a flower outside. She also painted scenes from the southwestern United States, where dry hills and wide skies gave her other shapes and colors to look at.
facts: Georgia O’Keeffe spent many years living and working in New Mexico.

entries.title: How did M. C. Escher make shapes fit together?
entries.answer: M. C. Escher made prints in which groups of shapes fit together like tiles. He could turn an ordinary outline into something that looks like a fish or another animal and still have the edges fit its neighbors. In some pictures the shapes get smaller and smaller near the edge. The change in size can make a flat design feel as if it goes on farther than the paper does.
facts: An arrangement like this can cover a surface without leaving gaps.

entries.title: How do watercolors make light colors?
entries.answer: With watercolors, a brush carries small bits of color mixed with water. A thin layer lets light reach the white paper and bounce back, so the paper helps the color look bright or pale. Artists can brush water over a large area before adding color to make it spread softly. When one layer dries, they can paint over it to build a stronger color or add sharp lines.
facts: A thin layer of watercolor spread across an area is called a wash.

entries.title: How does a woodcut make a picture?
entries.answer: To make a woodcut, an artist carves away the parts of a flat block that should stay blank on the picture. The raised parts that are left get covered with ink. Press paper against them and the ink moves to the paper. You can see the same idea in a stamp, where only the raised parts make a mark. One carved block can print several pictures. The print faces the opposite way from the block, so a letter on the block must be reversed to read correctly on paper.
facts: A woodcut is a kind of relief printing.
Artists can print with different blocks to add different colors.

entries.title: How does soft clay become a hard pot?
entries.answer: Wet clay can be pressed, rolled, or shaped as a wheel turns. A potter lets the finished shape dry before putting it into a special oven called a kiln. The heat changes the clay so it becomes hard and keeps its shape. A potter can add a coating called a glaze and heat the pot again. Some glazes melt into a smooth, glassy layer as they are fired.
facts: Many clay pots are shaped by hand, without a wheel.

entries.title: How does stop-motion make objects look alive?
entries.answer: Set a toy on a table, take a picture, and move it a tiny bit. Take another picture and repeat. Play the pictures quickly in order and the toy can look like it is moving by itself. Stop-motion animation uses lots of photographs made this way. Small changes between photos make the movement look smoother. Bumping the camera by accident can make the whole scene seem to jump.
facts: One still picture in an animation is called a frame.

entries.title: How does weaving turn threads into cloth?
entries.answer: A weaver stretches one set of threads in order. Those threads are the warp. Another thread, the weft, passes across them, going over some and under others. Each trip adds one row. The crossing threads hold one another in place. A loom helps keep the warp threads tight and makes room for the weft to pass through. Changing the colors or which threads go above others can make patterns.
facts: The warp and weft run in different directions across a woven cloth.

entries.title: How is a sculpture different from a drawing?
entries.answer: A sculpture takes up space that you can measure in three directions: height, width, and depth. You might walk around a statue and see different details on each side. A sculptor can carve away parts of a block, add pieces of clay, or join materials together. Some sculptures have a flat back and rise from a wall or a plaque, so you usually look at them from one side.
facts: Carving removes material, and modeling can add or reshape material.

entries.title: What can a portrait tell us?
entries.answer: A portrait is an artwork about a person or group of people. It could be a painting, a photograph, a drawing, or a sculpture. An artist can show more than a face. A runner holding a worn pair of shoes might suggest years of practice. A picture of someone at their kitchen table might tell a different story about the same person than a picture on a stage. Looking at choices such as the pose, clothes, and setting can help you see what the artist wanted you to notice.
facts: The person shown in a portrait is sometimes called the subject or sitter.
When an artist makes a portrait of themself, it is called a self-portrait.

entries.title: What did Frida Kahlo put into her self-portraits?
entries.answer: Frida Kahlo was a Mexican painter who often used herself as the person in a picture. She chose clothes, plants, objects, and settings that help tell the viewer something about her life and the ideas that mattered to her. A painter can see their own appearance in a mirror, but a self-portrait can also include details that a mirror would not show. That is one way an artist can tell a story without using a sentence.
facts: Kahlo’s family home in Mexico City is now a museum often called the Blue House.

entries.title: What is a landscape painting?
entries.answer: A landscape artwork shows a view of a place. It might show hills, a river, fields, or a busy town. The part that seems nearest is the foreground, and the part that seems farthest is the background. An artist can use large, clear shapes close to us and smaller, softer ones farther away. The view can feel wide and deep even if the paper is small and flat.
facts: Changing where the horizon sits can change how much sky or ground you see.

entries.title: What is a still life in art?
entries.answer: A still life is an artwork about objects such as a bowl, a book, flowers, or fruit. An artist can put the objects close to one another so their shapes overlap, or spread them out so we notice each one. Moving the light to one side can make the shadows longer and change which details stand out. Even the same cup can look different when you move your chair and draw it from a new place.
facts: Artists can show ordinary objects in a still life, including cups, food, and tools.

entries.title: What makes a picture a collage?
entries.answer: A collage is made by arranging pieces of material on a surface and attaching them. The pieces might be colored paper, scraps of cloth, photographs, or something else. A strip from an old map could become a roadway in a new picture, even though it once showed a river. Artists decide how edges overlap and where to leave empty space. Those choices can make separate pieces look like they belong together.
facts: A collage can use pieces with different textures, thicknesses, and colors.

entries.title: Why did Jacob Lawrence tell one history in many paintings?
entries.answer: Jacob Lawrence painted a series about the movement of many Black Americans from the South to other regions of the United States. One picture can show a train station, another a room, another a group waiting for work. Each painting gives one small part of a longer story. A visitor can use the pictures and their captions to think about the different reasons people moved and what they hoped to find.
facts: The Migration Series has sixty panels.

entries.title: Why did Van Gogh paint several sunflower pictures?
entries.answer: Vincent van Gogh made several paintings of sunflowers in jars and vases. Some use lots of yellow, yet the light and dark yellows still let you pick out the petals, flower heads, and background. The flowers can look lively or dried out depending on which bloom you look at. Comparing two versions helps you see how an artist can change the balance of colors without choosing a completely different subject.
facts: Some of Van Gogh’s sunflower paintings were made while he lived in Arles, in southern France.

entries.title: Why do distant objects look smaller in pictures?
entries.answer: Stand at one end of a long hallway. The walls get closer together in your view as they get farther away. You know the hallway stays the same width. Drawing its edges so they slant toward a point makes a picture feel like the real view. Artists call this kind of drawing linear perspective. The point where drawn lines appear to meet is called a vanishing point.
facts: Lines that seem to meet in a picture may be parallel in the real world.

entries.title: Why does Hokusai’s Great Wave look so large?
entries.answer: In Hokusai’s print of a great wave off Kanagawa, the dark blue wave curls over boats close to the front of the picture. Japan’s Mount Fuji looks tiny in the background, although a mountain is much bigger than a wave. Those sizes make sense because the boats and breaking wave are shown much nearer to the viewer. The picture was printed from carved blocks, so artists could make more than one copy.
facts: Hokusai’s print is often called The Great Wave.

entries.title: Why does the Mona Lisa’s face look so softly shaded?
entries.answer: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa as a portrait. Around the eyes and mouth, the changes from light to dark are very gentle. Hard edges would give the face a more sharply drawn look. Farther back, a landscape of rocks and water seems to stretch beyond the person in the chair. Looking from the face to the landscape lets you see two different uses of soft detail in the same painting.
facts: The Louvre in Paris keeps the Mona Lisa.

entries.title: Why doesn’t some art look like real things?
entries.answer: Some artists start with a real object and change its shapes, colors, or details. A bicycle might become a few circles and slanting lines. Other artists make patterns and marks without choosing a real object to show. Both can be kinds of abstract art. Look for colors that seem to push forward, shapes that repeat, and changes in the speed or direction of lines. You can notice those choices even without naming an object.
facts: An abstract artwork can show motion or a feeling through color, shape, or line.
